questions.q: What is the Navigator in Oracle Fusion Cloud?
options: The master menu listing every work area a signed-in user has access to, organized by product family
A GPS-style feature for mobile users
A report showing recent quarterly updates
A security role assigned only to administrators
questions.explain: The Navigator is the complete directory of work areas a user can access, opened from an icon in the global header and grouped by product family.

questions.q: What does 'simplified UI' refer to in Oracle Fusion Cloud?
options: A paid add-on feature
Oracle's modern, click-driven interface design, built with fewer fields visible at once compared to older dense forms
A version of Fusion Cloud with fewer modules
A simplified pricing plan
questions.explain: Simplified UI describes the modern, guided, click-driven design Oracle built Fusion Cloud around, in contrast to older dense-form software like E-Business Suite.

questions.q: Which older Oracle product is used in this lesson as an example of the dense, form-based interface style Fusion Cloud moved away from?
options: Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM
Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM
Oracle E-Business Suite
Oracle Visual Builder
questions.explain: E-Business Suite, being older on-premises software, is cited as an example of the dense, keyboard-driven form style that Fusion's simplified UI moved away from.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'Favorites' and 'Recent Items'?
options: They are the same feature with two different names
Recent Items can only show work areas, while Favorites can only show reports
Favorites are set by the administrator only; Recent Items are set by the user
Favorites are user-marked shortcuts; Recent Items are automatically tracked based on what a user just visited
questions.explain: Favorites are deliberately marked by the user, while Recent Items are automatically tracked by the system based on recent activity.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does navigation skill matter for a Financials consultant specifically?
options: Because most business processes span multiple work areas, so a consultant who navigates well — and can teach it — delivers more value
Because the exam only tests navigation
Because navigation has nothing to do with training end users
Because the Navigator cannot be customized at all
questions.explain: Since most business processes cross several work areas, understanding navigation and being able to explain it during training is real, practical value a consultant adds.
